subtitle: Understanding how pre-choruses build harmonic and rhythmic momentum toward the chorus

introduction.title: The Pre-Chorus: Building Momentum and Expectation
introduction.text: The pre-chorus serves as a crucial transitional section that bridges the gap between verse and chorus, both harmonically and energetically. It creates momentum, builds tension, and sets up the chorus for maximum impact. Understanding pre-chorus construction reveals how composers create forward motion and make chorus arrivals feel both inevitable and exciting.

columns.title: Energy Bridge
columns.text: Transitions between verse and chorus energy levels

columns.title: Chorus Setup
columns.text: Prepares harmonic and emotional context for chorus

cards.title: Tension Building
cards.description: Creates harmonic and rhythmic momentum toward the chorus

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Often uses progressions that avoid tonic, building expectation for chorus resolution

items: Ascending bass lines
Increased subdivision
Sequential progressions
Vocal range expansion

cards.title: Dynamic Bridge
cards.description: Transitions energy level from verse to chorus

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Serves as musical "ramp" between contrasting energy levels

items: Gradual volume increase
Instrumental additions
Rhythmic intensification

cards.title: Harmonic Preparation
cards.description: Sets up the harmonic context for the chorus

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Establishes dominant or predominant harmony to make chorus tonic arrival powerful

items: Dominant prolongation
Circle of fifths movement
Secondary dominants

cards.title: Lyrical Setup
cards.description: Provides narrative or emotional setup for chorus message

fields.label: Theory
fields.value: Creates lyrical momentum that makes chorus feel inevitable and necessary

items: Question-answer structure
Emotional escalation
Perspective shift

cards.title: Length

fields.label: Typical Range
fields.value: 2-8 bars

fields.label: Key Consideration
fields.value: Long enough to build momentum, short enough to maintain urgency

items: 4 bars most common
8 bars for extended builds
2 bars for quick transitions

cards.title: Harmonic Rhythm

fields.label: Typical Range
fields.value: Faster than verse, similar to or slower than chorus

fields.label: Key Consideration
fields.value: Should accelerate harmonic motion toward chorus

items: One chord per beat vs. verse two beats per chord
Faster changes create urgency

cards.title: Melodic Range

fields.label: Typical Range
fields.value: Higher than verse, approaches or exceeds chorus range

fields.label: Key Consideration
fields.value: Bridges the vocal register gap between sections

items: Ascending melodic lines
Gradual range expansion
Peak notes approach chorus

cards.title: Rhythmic Density

fields.label: Typical Range
fields.value: Increased subdivision and activity

fields.label: Key Consideration
fields.value: More active than verse to build energy

items: Eighth notes vs. quarter notes
Drum fills
Busier bass lines

cards.title: Dominant Prolongation
cards.description: When strong, decisive chorus entry is needed

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: V/V - V - V7

fields.label: Example
fields.value: D - G - G7 (in C major)

fields.label: Harmonic Function
fields.value: Extends dominant harmony to build maximum tension

fields.label: Chorus Resolution
fields.value: Resolves powerfully to I in chorus

cards.title: Ascending Sequential
cards.description: Creates sense of inevitable forward motion

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: vi - IV - V - V/V

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Am - F - G - D (in C major)

fields.label: Harmonic Function
fields.value: Builds through circle of fifths motion

fields.label: Chorus Resolution
fields.value: Natural momentum leads to chorus

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: I - ♭II - ii - V

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C - D♭ - Dm - G (in C major)

fields.label: Harmonic Function
fields.value: Half-step bass motion creates rising energy

fields.label: Chorus Resolution
fields.value: Strong V-I cadence into chorus

cards.title: Relative Minor Escape
cards.description: When contrast between dark pre-chorus and bright chorus is wanted

fields.label: Progression
fields.value: vi - IV - V

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Am - F - G (in C major)

fields.label: Harmonic Function
fields.value: Starts in relative minor, moves to dominant preparation

fields.label: Chorus Resolution
fields.value: Brightness of major chorus feels like emergence

cards.title: Standard Pre-Chorus
cards.description: Traditional placement between verse and chorus

fields.label: Structure
fields.value: Verse → Pre-Chorus → Chorus

fields.label: Common In
fields.value: Most common in pop, rock, and contemporary music

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Smooth energy transition and harmonic preparation

cards.title: Double Pre-Chorus
cards.description: Two distinct pre-chorus sections with building intensity

fields.label: Structure
fields.value: Verse → Pre-Chorus 1 → Pre-Chorus 2 → Chorus

fields.label: Common In
fields.value: Epic ballads, progressive rock, dramatic builds

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Extended tension building for maximum chorus impact

cards.title: Pre-Chorus Only
cards.description: Pre-chorus appears before some but not all choruses

fields.label: Structure
fields.value: Verse → Pre-Chorus → Verse → Chorus

fields.label: Common In
fields.value: When different approaches to chorus are desired

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates structural variation and surprise

fields.label: Structure
fields.value: Verse → Extended Pre-Chorus → Chorus

fields.label: Common In
fields.value: Progressive music, complex arrangements

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Substantial bridge between verse and chorus energies

cards.title: Vocal Range Expansion

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Verse: C4-G4 → Pre-chorus: G4-C5

fields.label: Detail
fields.value: Gradual upward movement

items: Systematically expanding vocal range through the pre-chorus builds excitement and sets up chorus high notes naturally.

cards.title: Rhythmic Acceleration

fields.label: Detail
fields.value: Increasing subdivision density

items: Progressive increase in rhythmic activity creates forward momentum and makes the chorus arrival feel like a release.

cards.title: Harmonic Acceleration

fields.label: Example
fields.value: 2 chords/bar → 1 chord/bar → 2 chords/bar

fields.label: Detail
fields.value: Faster harmonic rhythm

items: Increasing the rate of chord changes creates urgency and makes the chorus feel like the natural destination.

cards.title: Dynamic Builds

fields.label: Example
fields.value: mf → f → ff (into chorus)

fields.label: Detail
fields.value: Progressive volume increase

items: Systematic volume increases through the pre-chorus create anticipation and make chorus arrival more impactful.

cards.title: Musical Elements
items: Harmonic progression: How does it build toward chorus?
Melodic direction: Does melody ascend or build energy?
Rhythmic activity: How does subdivision change?
Dynamic progression: How does volume/intensity grow?
Length and pacing: Does timing feel appropriate?

cards.title: Functional Analysis
items: Momentum creation: Does it successfully build energy?
Tension building: Is expectation for chorus created?
Transition quality: How smooth is the flow to chorus?
Harmonic preparation: Does it set up chorus effectively?
Structural necessity: Does the song need this section?
